duchess-of-oldenburg.heading: BOROVITSKY
duchess-of-oldenburg.flavour: Flesh white, firm, juicy, with a sweet, brisk, sub-acid, very pleasant flavour.
duchess-of-oldenburg.storage: An early dessert fruit, ripe the middle of August.
duchess-of-oldenburg.note: Described as Borovitsky (in our aka), sent from the Taurida Gardens, St. Petersburg, in 1824. Lindley does not mention Duchess of Oldenburg; Hogg 1851 keeps Borovitsky and Duchess of Oldenburgh apart.

irish-peach.heading: IRISH PEACH APPLE
irish-peach.flavour: Flesh white, tender, juicy, rich, and very highly flavoured.
irish-peach.storage: A dessert apple, ripe in August.

arbroath-pippin.heading: OSLIN
arbroath-pippin.flavour: Flesh inclining to yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, very rich, and highly flavoured.
arbroath-pippin.storage: Ripe about the middle of August
arbroath-pippin.note: Synonyms Oslin Pippin, Oslin or Arbroath Pippin (Forsyth), Orgeline.

red-astrachan.heading: RED ASTRACAN
red-astrachan.flavour: Flesh white, crisp. Juice abundant, with a rich saccharine acid, but soon becomes mealy.
red-astrachan.storage: Ripe about the middle of August. ... but soon becomes mealy.

devonshire-quarrenden.heading: RED QUARENDEN
devonshire-quarrenden.flavour: Flesh greenish white; when newly gathered, crisp, very juicy, mixed with a most agreeable acid.
devonshire-quarrenden.quality: very much and very justly esteemed
devonshire-quarrenden.storage: Ripe in August, and will keep till the end of September.
devonshire-quarrenden.note: Described as Red Quarenden; synonyms Devonshire Quarenden, Sack apple. Lindley finds the name unknown in Devonshire; common in Somerset and Gloucestershire.

emperor-alexander.heading: EMPEROR ALEXANDER
emperor-alexander.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, crisp, and very tender. Juice sugary, and of a rich aromatic flavour.
emperor-alexander.storage: An autumnal dessert apple from October till nearly Christmas.
emperor-alexander.note: Synonyms Alexander, Aporta; fruit imported from Riga in 1817. Same entry recorded for our 'aport'.

aport.heading: EMPEROR ALEXANDER
aport.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, crisp, and very tender. Juice sugary, and of a rich aromatic flavour.
aport.storage: An autumnal dessert apple from October till nearly Christmas.
aport.note: Lindley gives 'Aporta' (after the Hort. Soc. Catalogue) as a synonym of Emperor Alexander; same entry as our 'emperor-alexander'. Probable only.

flower-of-kent.heading: FLOWER OF KENT
flower-of-kent.flavour: Flesh greenish yellow, with a pretty good juice.

summer-rambo.heading: FRANK RAMBOUR
summer-rambo.flavour: Flesh rather soft, with a slightly acid juice.
summer-rambo.note: Synonyms Rambour Franc, Rambour Gros. Lindley does not name it Rambour d'Ete; the tie to our Summer Rambo comes from Hogg 1851, who lists 'Rambour d'Ete or Summer Rambour' under Rambour Franc.

hawthornden.heading: HAWTHORNDEN
hawthornden.flavour: Flesh white. Juice plentiful, and well flavoured.
hawthornden.quality: An excellent culinary fruit ... This is a very valuable apple, and a most excellent bearer.

kerry-pippin.heading: KERRY PIPPIN
kerry-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, tender, juicy, sugary, and high flavoured.
kerry-pippin.note: Long known in County Kerry; best on the Doucin stock as an espalier.

kentish-fillbasket.heading: POTTER'S LARGE APPLE
kentish-fillbasket.flavour: Flesh white. Juice not plentiful, sub-acid.
kentish-fillbasket.storage: A culinary apple from Michaelmas to Christmas
kentish-fillbasket.note: Described as Potter's Large Apple (raised by a Mr. Potter of Chelsea); the tie to Kentish Fillbasket is through our aka only.

wyken-pippin.heading: WYKEN PIPPIN
wyken-pippin.flavour: Flesh greenish yellow, firm, crisp. Juice sugary, with a little musky perfume.
wyken-pippin.note: Original tree seen at Wyken near Coventry in May 1827.

yellow-ingestrie.heading: YELLOW INGESTRIE
yellow-ingestrie.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, very tender and delicate. Juice plentiful, rich, and highly flavoured.
yellow-ingestrie.note: Raised by Mr. Knight. Lindley's Summer Golden Pippin (line 1480; in our aka) is a separate entry: 'sweet and agreeable, without perfume'.

beauty-of-kent.heading: BEAUTY OF KENT
beauty-of-kent.flavour: Flesh firm, yellowish white, crisp, and tender. Juice abundant, and pleasantly acid. ... although not distinguished by any peculiar richness of flavour, it certainly must be reckoned a very excellent fruit.
beauty-of-kent.quality: it certainly must be reckoned a very excellent fruit.
beauty-of-kent.storage: An autumnal dessert apple, from Michaelmas to Christmas.
beauty-of-kent.note: Lindley treats it as a dessert apple.

keswick-codlin.heading: KESWICK CODLIN
keswick-codlin.flavour: Flesh pale yellow. Juice plentiful, subacid.
keswick-codlin.storage: A culinary apple from September to November. ... Its young fruit may be gathered for tarts in the month of June
keswick-codlin.note: Recommended with Hawthornden for the cottager's garden.

king-of-the-pippins.heading: KING OF THE PIPPINS
king-of-the-pippins.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, firm, breaking, very sweet, juicy, and highly flavoured.
king-of-the-pippins.quality: A very beautiful dessert fruit ... This very excellent apple
king-of-the-pippins.note: Synonym Hampshire Yellow; brought into notice by Kirke of Brompton (the apple Hogg 1851 calls Golden Winter Pearmain).

manks-codlin.heading: MANKS CODLIN
manks-codlin.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, very firm. Juice brisk, subacid, with a slight aromatic flavour.

sops-in-wine.heading: SOPS OF WINE
sops-in-wine.flavour: Flesh soft, white, tinctured more or less with pale red to the core. ... Juice sweet, but not rich.
sops-in-wine.storage: A culinary apple in October and November.
sops-in-wine.note: Synonyms Sops in Wine (Ray), Rode Wyn Appel (Knoop).

autumn-pearmain.heading: SUMMER PEARMAIN
autumn-pearmain.flavour: Flesh pale yellow, crisp, firm. Juice not plentiful, but rich, and of a high aromatic flavour.
autumn-pearmain.quality: A most excellent and beautiful dessert apple
autumn-pearmain.storage: from October till Christmas. In some seasons, however, it is in perfection in September.
autumn-pearmain.note: Described as Summer Pearmain (in our aka); synonyms Parmain d'Ete and the Royal Pearmain of Forsyth and the London nurserymen.

blenheim-orange.heading: BLENHEIM PIPPIN
blenheim-orange.flavour: Flesh yellow, breaking, sweet, juicy, extremely pleasant, and high flavoured.
blenheim-orange.quality: one of the largest of our table apples
blenheim-orange.storage: A dessert apple from November till March.

caroline.heading: CAROLINE APPLE
caroline.flavour: Flesh firm, with a brisk juice and high flavour.
caroline.note: Named after Caroline, lady of the late Lord Suffield; Lindley calls it culinary.

cornish-aromatic.heading: CORNISH AROMATIC
cornish-aromatic.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, juicy, with an exceedingly rich, high, aromatic flavour.
cornish-aromatic.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.

court-pendu-plat.heading: COURTPENDU
court-pendu-plat.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, with a rich, lively, agreeable flavour.
court-pendu-plat.quality: one of the handsomest and best of our table apples
court-pendu-plat.storage: A dessert apple from November till March.
court-pendu-plat.note: Synonyms Capendu (Duhamel), Courtpendu Plat, Garnon's Apple.

dumelows-seedling.heading: DUMELOW'S SEEDLING
dumelows-seedling.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, with a brisk acid juice.

golden-noble.heading: GOLDEN NOBLE
golden-noble.flavour: Flesh yellow, tender, with a pleasant sub-acid juice. ... It bakes of a fine, clear amber colour, perfectly melting, with a rich acidity.
golden-noble.storage: A culinary apple from November till March.
golden-noble.note: Old tree near Downham Market; shown 1820.

london-pippin.heading: LONDON PIPPIN
london-pippin.flavour: Flesh firm, crisp, of a yellowish white. Juice plentiful, sub-acid, of a good flavour.
london-pippin.quality: the most common and best known of any in the Norwich market
london-pippin.storage: A culinary sort from October till January.
london-pippin.note: Synonym Five-crowned Pippin; Lindley calls it 'a real Norfolk apple'.

margil.heading: MARGIL
margil.flavour: Flesh yellow, firm, breaking. Juice sweet, with a high aromatic flavour.
margil.storage: A dessert fruit from November till March.
margil.note: Lindley's separate 'Fail-me-never' / Never-fail (line 3406, a red Scottish culinary apple) is not Margil, though Never Fail is in our aka.

newtown-pippin.heading: NEWTOWN PIPPIN
newtown-pippin.flavour: Flesh pale yellow, or yellowish white, firm. Juice saccharine, and possessing an exceedingly rich and highly aromatic flavour.
newtown-pippin.storage: In eating from December till April.
newtown-pippin.note: Synonym American Newtown Pippin; described from fruit grown at Chiswick in 1830.

norfolk-beefing.heading: NORFOLK BEAUFIN
norfolk-beefing.flavour: Flesh very firm. Juice not plentiful, sub-acid.
norfolk-beefing.storage: A culinary apple from November till May or June.
norfolk-beefing.climate: The trees, being somewhat tender, require to be planted on a good soil and in a warm situation, otherwise they are apt to canker and become short lived.
norfolk-beefing.note: Heading OCR 'NORFOLK BEAUFIX'; synonym Norfolk Beefin. Dried by Norwich bakers.

calville-blanc-dhiver.heading: WINTER WHITE CALVILLE
calville-blanc-dhiver.flavour: Flesh white and tender, with a very pleasant juice.
calville-blanc-dhiver.storage: A culinary apple from December till March.
calville-blanc-dhiver.note: Synonyms Calville Blanche d'Hiver, Bonnet Carre.

adams-pearmain.heading: ADAMS'S PEARMAIN
adams-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp. Juice saccharine, rich, with a very high aromatic flavour.
adams-pearmain.quality: a very handsome and most excellent apple, and highly deserving of cultivation
adams-pearmain.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.

esopus-spitzenburg.heading: AESOPUS SPITZEMBERG
esopus-spitzenburg.flavour: Flesh yellow, very rich, juicy, and brisk.
esopus-spitzenburg.quality: A most excellent apple of American origin
esopus-spitzenburg.climate: It is too tender to succeed in this country, without the assistance of a south or an east wall.

catshead.heading: CATSHEAD
catshead.storage: A culinary apple from October till January.
catshead.note: Lindley gives Costard (Ray) and Coustard as synonyms; Hogg 1851 says this is an error, so the entry is not recorded for our 'costard'.

claygate-pearmain.heading: CLAYGATE PEARMAIN
claygate-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellow, rather dry, like all apples of this class, but sweet and very rich.
claygate-pearmain.quality: a valuable addition to our stock of table apples
claygate-pearmain.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.
claygate-pearmain.note: First shown by John Braddick, December 1821.

cockle-pippin.heading: COCKLE PIPPIN
cockle-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, and tender. Juice saccharine, mixed with acid, and a slight pleasant perfume.
cockle-pippin.quality: A dessert apple, and also excellent for culinary purposes
cockle-pippin.note: Synonyms Nutmeg Cockle Pippin, Nutmeg Pippin, White Cockle.

cornish-gilliflower.heading: CORNISH GILLIFLOWER
cornish-gilliflower.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, and very rich; when cut, it gives out a pleasant perfume, resembling the Clove Gilliflower, whence its name.
cornish-gilliflower.storage: A dessert apple, ripening in November, and will keep till April.
cornish-gilliflower.note: The perfume is compared to the Clove Gilliflower (clove pink), a flower scent. Synonyms Julyflower, Cornish Julyflower, Calville d'Angleterre.

gravenstein.heading: GRAVENSTEIN
gravenstein.flavour: Flesh pale yellow, crisp, with a high-flavoured vinous juice.
gravenstein.quality: may be reckoned a rival to our Ribston Pippin
gravenstein.storage: A dessert apple, ripening in the autumn, but will keep till April
gravenstein.note: Esteemed the best apple in Germany and the Low Countries; first shown 1819.

colonel-vaughan.heading: KENTISH PIPPIN
colonel-vaughan.flavour: Flesh yellowish white. Juice sweetish, or sub-acid, with a smart pungent flavour.
colonel-vaughan.quality: An excellent culinary apple ... an old favourite kitchen apple
colonel-vaughan.storage: An excellent culinary apple from October till January.
colonel-vaughan.note: Described as Kentish Pippin (in our aka);Lindley has no Colonel Vaughan entry, and Hogg 1851 keeps Colonel Vaughan's and Kentish Pippin apart. Lindley says it is not the Kentish Pippin of Forsyth.

lemon-pippin.heading: LEMON PIPPIN
lemon-pippin.flavour: Flesh firm, breaking. Juice not abundant, nor high flavoured, but very pleasant.
lemon-pippin.storage: A dessert fruit from October till March.

ribston-pippin.heading: RIBSTON PIPPIN
ribston-pippin.flavour: Flesh pale yellow, firm, crisp. Juice saccharine, with a pungent, rich, and delicious aromatic flavour.
ribston-pippin.quality: one of the best, and certainly is one of the most popular dessert apples of the present day
ribston-pippin.storage: A dessert apple from October till April, but it is generally in its greatest perfection when it has been gathered a month or six weeks.
ribston-pippin.note: Synonyms Formosa Pippin, Traver's Apple, Glory of York.

winter-pearmain.heading: WINTER PEARMAIN
winter-pearmain.flavour: Flesh pale green, firm, crisp. Juice not plentiful, but saccharine, and of a slight aromatic flavour.
winter-pearmain.storage: A dessert apple from November till March.
winter-pearmain.note: Synonyms Old Pearmain, Parmain d'Hiver, Pepin Parmain d'Angleterre. Cross-referenced again in the cider section (line 6609).

calville-rouge-dhiver.heading: WINTER RED CALVILLE
calville-rouge-dhiver.flavour: Flesh tender, with an agreeable juice.
calville-rouge-dhiver.storage: A culinary apple from November till February.
calville-rouge-dhiver.note: Synonyms Calville Rouge, Calville Rouge d'Hiver.

aromatic-russet.heading: AROMATIC RUSSET
aromatic-russet.flavour: Flesh greenish white, firm, crisp, but tender. Juice saccharine and perfumed.
aromatic-russet.quality: a very hardy sort, and an excellent bearer
aromatic-russet.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.
aromatic-russet.note: Homonym doubt: Lindley's Aromatic Russet is 'not of Hort. Soc. Cat. 1061'; he puts Spice Apple and Rook's-nest Apple (both in our aka) under Fenouillet Gris (line 5451), 'often sold under the name of Aromatic Russet'. Hogg 1851 cites this Lindley entry for his Aromatic Russet.

ashmeads-kernel.heading: ASHMEAD'S KERNEL
ashmeads-kernel.flavour: Flesh firm and crisp. Juice plentiful, of an excellent and rich aromatic flavour.
ashmeads-kernel.quality: A very neat dessert apple ... a very valuable and hardy variety, highly deserving of cultivation.
ashmeads-kernel.note: Lindley believes it a seedling of the Nonpareil.

braddick-nonpareil.heading: BRADDICK'S NONPAREIL
braddick-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh yellowish, sweeter and more melting than the old Nonpareil, with a richly sugared and slightly aromatic juice.
braddick-nonpareil.storage: A dessert apple from October till Christmas.
braddick-nonpareil.note: Raised by John Braddick at Thames Ditton.

knobby-russet.heading: KNOBBY RUSSET
knobby-russet.flavour: Flesh yellowish, crisp, not juicy, but sweet and high flavoured.
knobby-russet.quality: It is a valuable fruit, and extremely hardy.
knobby-russet.storage: A dessert apple from November till May.

nonpareil.heading: OLD NONPAREIL
nonpareil.flavour: Flesh very firm, crisp. Juice not plentiful, but of a most singularly rich, poignant, aromatic flavour.
nonpareil.quality: One of our most admired dessert apples
nonpareil.storage: in its greatest perfection from Christmas to Lady-day.
nonpareil.climate: when grafted upon the Doucin stock, upon a good soil, and under judicious management, their fruit has been as perfect as the best of our newest productions.

ross-nonpareil.heading: ROSS NONPAREIL
ross-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh firm, greenish white, sweet and rich, with an agreeable perfumed fennel flavour. ... one of the few fennel-flavoured apples which are cultivated among us.
ross-nonpareil.storage: A dessert fruit from November till April.
ross-nonpareil.climate: It is a great bearer, and healthy on all soils

sam-young.heading: SAM YOUNG
sam-young.flavour: Flesh inclining to yellow, mixed with green; tender, and melting. Juice plentiful, sweet, with a delicious flavour, scarcely inferior to that of the Golden Pippin.
sam-young.quality: An Irish dessert apple, of high reputation ... certainly one of the best of our modern apples
sam-young.storage: ripe in November, and will keep good for two months.
sam-young.note: Synonym Irish Russet; made known in 1818 by Mr. Robertson of Kilkenny.

wheelers-russet.heading: WHEELER'S RUSSET
wheelers-russet.flavour: Flesh firm, greenish white. Juice not plentiful, but of a brisk, saccharine, aromatic flavour, charged with acid.
wheelers-russet.storage: A dessert and culinary apple from November till May. ... when highly ripened and beginning to shrivel, is one of the best russets of its season.

hagloe-crab.heading: HAGLOE CRAB
hagloe-crab.quality: produces a most excellent cider, both of strength and body
hagloe-crab.climate: when planted on a dry soil, with a calcareous bottom, in a warm situation and season, produces a most excellent cider

hereford-redstreak.heading: REDSTREAK
hereford-redstreak.quality: the first fine cider apple that was cultivated in Herefordshire, or probably in England
hereford-redstreak.note: Cider section; juice specific gravity 1079; called Scudamore's Crab when first cultivated.

alfriston.heading: ALFRISTON
alfriston.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, very crisp and tender. Juice plentiful, saccharine, combined with a smart brisk acid.
alfriston.quality: A very fine and excellent culinary apple
alfriston.note: Lindley gives the season as October till Christmas (Hogg: November to April). Sometimes wrongly called Newtown Pippin.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFF
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, firm, crisp. Juice sugary, with a singularly musky perfume.
edelborsdorfer.quality: a German apple of very excellent quality
edelborsdorfer.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.
edelborsdorfer.note: Synonyms Borsdorffer, Reinette batarde, Postophe d'Hiver, Bursdoff or Queen's Apple. A favourite of Queen Charlotte; specimen brought from Leipsic in 1798.

reinette-du-canada.heading: CANADIAN REINETTE
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, firm, juicy, with a high, brisk, sub-acid flavour.
reinette-du-canada.storage: in December, and keeps well till March.
reinette-du-canada.note: Synonyms Reinette de Canada, Grosse Reinette d'Angleterre, Reinette de Canada blanche, Reinette de Canada a Cotes, Portugal apple, Janurea. Often sold in London as Newtown Pippin.

dutch-mignonne.heading: DUTCH MIGNONNE
dutch-mignonne.flavour: Flesh very firm, crisp. Juice plentiful, with a delicious aromatic, sub-acid flavour.
dutch-mignonne.storage: A dessert apple from November till May or June.
dutch-mignonne.note: Synonyms Christ's Golden Reinette, Reinette Doree, Pomme de Laak, Paternoster Apple. Brought from Holland to Catton near Norwich by Thomas Harvey.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh yellow, firm, breaking, very rich, juicy, spicy, and high flavoured.
golden-harvey.quality: A most excellent and beautiful dessert apple
golden-harvey.storage: ripening in December, and keeping till May or June.

holland-pippin.heading: HOLLAND PIPPIN
holland-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, pretty firm, tender. Juice sub-acid, mixed with a good deal of sugar, and a slight perfume.
holland-pippin.note: Miller's Holland Pippin (the one Hogg accepts as the true Holland Pippin); no Kirton synonym given.

lucombes-seedling.heading: LUCOMBE'S SEEDLING
lucombes-seedling.flavour: Flesh whitish, firm, juicy, and agreeable, but not high flavoured.
lucombes-seedling.storage: from October till February or March.
lucombes-seedling.note: Raised by Mr. Lucombe of Exeter.

baxters-pearmain.heading: BAXTER'S PEARMAIN
baxters-pearmain.flavour: Flesh firm. Juice saccharine, and well flavoured.
baxters-pearmain.storage: A culinary apple from November till March.
baxters-pearmain.note: A real Norfolk apple, in general cultivation throughout the county.

ortley.heading: ORTLEY APPLE
ortley.flavour: Flesh inclining to yellow, crisp, and breaking. Juice plentiful, with the same fine flavour which distinguishes the Newtown Pippin.
ortley.storage: A dessert apple from November till April.
ortley.note: Native of New Jersey; shown to the Horticultural Society in March 1825. Likened to the yellow Newtown Pippin.

fenouillet-gris.heading: FENOUILLET GRIS
fenouillet-gris.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, crisp, tender, with a saccharine and highly flavoured aromatic juice.
fenouillet-gris.storage: A dessert apple from November till February.
fenouillet-gris.note: Synonyms Anis, Caraway Russet, Spice Apple, Brown Apple of Burnt Island, Rook's-nest Apple; often sold in London as Aromatic Russet. This ties our Caraway Russet aka to Fenouillet Gris. Lindley does not mention anise beyond the synonym.

foxwhelp.heading: FOX-WHELP
foxwhelp.flavour: The expressed juice of this is extremely rich and saccharine, and enters, in a greater or less proportion, into the composition of many of the finest ciders now made in Herefordshire, to which it communicates both strength and flavour.
foxwhelp.note: Specific gravity of the juice 1076 to 1080. Known since Ray (1688); Knight believed it native to Herefordshire. No mention of acidity or astringency.

coccagee.heading: 195. COCCAGEE. Hort. Soc. Cat. 167, Cockagee. Forsyth, Ed. 3. No. 22.
coccagee.flavour: Flesh rather soft, yellowish white. Juice sharp acid, with an unpleasant astringency.
coccagee.quality: This apple produces the well known, and by some highly esteemed, Coccagee Cider.
coccagee.note: Lindley's fruit was pale lemon with no red; Forsyth described a red cheek.

styre.heading: 197. FOREST STYRE. Pom. Heref. t. 12. Red Styre. Ib.
styre.climate: is planted principally in the light soils, in the neighbourhood of the Forest of Dean, where it affords a stronger cider than the deeper soils of Herefordshire.
styre.note: 'The Styre, or Stire, is a native of Gloucestershire'; Philips's 'Stirom'. Styre cider kept thirty and forty years. No taste words.

woodcock.heading: 213. WOODCOCK APPLE. Pom. Heref. t. 10.
woodcock.quality: a cider apple of great excellence
woodcock.note: Praised by 17th-century writers; cultivation declining by 1831. No taste words.
